scope: Organizations (software producers and software acquirers)
policy_description: Organizations should integrate the SSDF throughout their existing software development practices, express their secure software development requirements to third-party suppliers using SSDF conventions, and acquire software that meets the practices described in the SSDF.

scope: Organizations (software producers and software acquirers)
policy_description: Organizations should ensure that their people, processes, and technology are prepared to perform secure software development.

scope: Organizations (software producers and software acquirers)
policy_description: Organizations should protect all components of their software from tampering and unauthorized access.

scope: Organizations (software producers and software acquirers)
policy_description: Organizations should produce well-secured software with minimal security vulnerabilities in its releases.

scope: Organizations (software producers and software acquirers)
policy_description: Organizations should identify residual vulnerabilities in their software releases and respond appropriately to address those vulnerabilities and prevent similar ones from occurring in the future.

scope: Organizations adopting the SSDF for their software development practices
policy_description: Organizations should adopt a risk-based approach to determine what practices are relevant, appropriate, and effective to mitigate the threats to their software development practices.

scope: Organization-level software development; may also apply to subsets of development groups or projects
policy_description: PO.1.1: Identify and document all security requirements for the organization’s software development, including development infrastructures and processes, and maintain the requirements over time.
reference: BSIMM: CP1.1, CP1.3, SR1.1, SR2.2, SE1.2, SE2.6
SCFPSSD: Planning the Implementation and Deployment of Secure Development Practices

scope: Organization-level software development; may also apply to subsets of development groups or projects
policy_description: PO.1.2: Identify and document all security requirements for organization-developed software to meet, and maintain the requirements over time.
reference: BSAFSS: SC.1-1, SC.2, PD.1-1, PD.1-2, PD.1-3, PD.2-2, SI, PA, CS, AA, LO, EE
OWASPSAMM: PC1-A, PC1-B, PC2-A, PC3-A, SR1-A, SR1-B, SR2-B, SA1-B, IR1-A
SCFPSSD: Establish Coding Standards and Conventions

scope: Organization-level software development; communication with third-party suppliers
policy_description: PO.1.3: Communicate requirements to all third parties who will provide commercial software components to the organization for reuse by the organization’s own software. [Formerly PW.3.1]
reference: SCAGILE: Tasks Requiring the Help of Security Experts 8
SCFPSSD: Manage Security Risk Inherent in the Use of Third-Party Components

scope: Organization-level software development; SDLC participants
policy_description: PO.2.1: Create new roles and alter responsibilities for existing roles as needed to encompass all parts of the software development SDLC. Periodically review and maintain the defined roles and responsibilities, updating them as needed.
reference: SCSIC: Vendor Software Development Integrity Controls

scope: Personnel with development-related responsibilities
policy_description: PO.2.2: Provide role-based training for all personnel with responsibilities that contribute to secure development. Periodically review personnel proficiency and role-based training, and update the training as needed.
reference: SCAGILE: Operational Security Tasks 14, 15; Tasks Requiring the Help of Security Experts 1
SCFPSSD: Planning the Implementation and Deployment of Secure Development Practices
SCSIC: Vendor Software Development Integrity Controls

scope: Organization leadership and authorizing officials for SDLC
policy_description: PO.2.3: Obtain upper management or authorizing official commitment to secure development, and convey that commitment to all with development-related roles and responsibilities.

scope: Organization-level toolchains used in software development
policy_description: PO.3.1: Specify which tools or tool types must or should be included in each toolchain to mitigate identified risks, as well as how the toolchain components are to be integrated with each other.
reference: CNCFSSCP: Securing Materials—Verification; Securing Build Pipelines—Verification, Automation, Secure Authentication/Access; Securing Artefacts—Verification; Securing Deployments—Verification
SCAGILE: Tasks Requiring the Help of Security Experts 9
SCSIC: Vendor Software Delivery Integrity Controls

scope: Tools and toolchains used during the SDLC
policy_description: PO.3.2: Follow recommended security practices to deploy, operate, and maintain tools and toolchains.
reference: CNCFSSCP: Securing Build Pipelines—Verification, Automation, Controlled Environments; Secure Authentication/Access; Securing Artefacts—Verification, Automation, Controlled Environments; Securing Deployments—Verification, Automation
SCAGILE: Tasks Requiring the Help of Security Experts 9
SCFPSSD: Use Current Compiler and Toolchain Versions and Secure Compiler Options
SCSIC: Vendor Software Delivery Integrity Controls

scope: Tools and automation used to support secure development
policy_description: PO.3.3: Configure tools to generate artifacts of their support of secure software development practices as defined by the organization.
reference: CNCFSSCP: Securing Build Pipelines—Verification, Automation, Controlled Environments; Securing Artefacts—Verification
SCAGILE: Tasks Requiring the Help of Security Experts 9
SCSIC: Vendor Software Delivery Integrity Controls

scope: Organization-level software security checks used during development
policy_description: PO.4.1: Define criteria for software security checks.
reference: BSIMM: SM1.4, SM2.1, SM2.2, SM2.6, SM3.3, CP2.2

scope: Organization-level software security criteria and associated data collection
policy_description: PO.4.2: Implement processes, mechanisms, etc. to gather and safeguard the necessary information in support of the criteria.
reference: IEC62443: SI-1, SVV-1, SVV-2, SVV-3, SVV-4
SCSIC: Vendor Software Delivery Integrity Controls

scope: Software development environments (development, build, test, staging, production, distribution)
policy_description: PO.5.1: Separate and protect each environment involved in software development.
reference: SCAGILE: Tasks Requiring the Help of Security Experts 11
SCSIC: Vendor Software Delivery Integrity Controls

scope: Development endpoints used by designers, developers, testers, builders, etc.
policy_description: PO.5.2: Secure and harden development endpoints (i.e., endpoints for software designers, developers, testers, builders, etc.) to perform development-related tasks using a risk-based approach.
reference: NISTCSF: PR.AC-4, PR.AC-7, PR.IP-1, PR.IP-3, PR.IP-12, PR.PT-1, PR.PT-3, DE.CM
SCAGILE: Tasks Requiring the Help of Security Experts 11
SCSIC: Vendor Software Delivery Integrity Controls

scope: All forms of code and related repositories used by the organization
policy_description: PS.1.1: Store all forms of code – including source code, executable code, and configuration-as-code – and restrict access to it based on the nature of the code.
reference: CNCFSSCP: Securing the Source Code—Verification, Automation, Controlled Environments, Secure Authentication
SCSIC: Vendor Software Delivery Integrity Controls, Vendor Software Development Integrity Controls

scope: Software releases and release artifacts provided to acquirers
policy_description: PS.2.1: Make software integrity verification information available to software acquirers.
reference: SCSIC: Vendor Software Delivery Integrity Controls

scope: Software releases and archival of release artifacts
policy_description: PS.3.1: Securely archive the necessary files and supporting data (e.g., integrity verification information, provenance data) to be retained for each software release.
reference: CNCFSSCP: Securing Artefacts—Automation, Controlled Environments, Encryption; Securing Deployments—Verification
SCSIC: Vendor Software Delivery Integrity Controls

scope: All components of each software release (including third-party components)
policy_description: PS.3.2: Collect, safeguard, maintain, and share provenance data for all components of each software release (e.g., in a software bill of materials [SBOM]).
reference: SCSIC: Vendor Software Delivery Integrity Controls

policy_description: PW.1.1: Use forms of risk modeling 	6 such as threat modeling, attack modeling, or attack surface mapping 	6 to help assess the security risk for the software.
reference: SCAGILE: Tasks Requiring the Help of Security Experts 3

policy_description: PW.1.2: Track and maintain the softwares security requirements, risks, and design decisions.

PW.1.3: Where appropriate, build in support for using standardized security features and services (e.g., enabling software to integrate with existing log management, identity management, access control, and vulnerability management systems) instead of creating proprietary implementations of security features and services.
reference: SCFPSSD: Standardize Identity and Access Management; Establish Log Requirements and Audit Practices

policy_description: PW.2.1: Have 1) a qualified person (or people) who were not involved with the design and/or instantiated in the toolchain review the software design to confirm and enforce that it meets all security requirements and satisfactorily addresses the identified risk information.

PW.4.1: Acquire and maintain well-secured software components (e.g., software libraries, modules, middleware, frameworks) from commercial, open-source, and other third-party developers for use by the organizations software.

scope: in-house created software components intended to meet common internal needs
policy_description: PW.4.2: Create and maintain well-secured software components in-house following SDLC processes to meet common internal software development needs that cannot be better met by third-party software components.
PW.4.4: Verify that acquired commercial, open-source, and all other third-party software components comply with the requirements, as defined by the organization, throughout their life cycles.
reference: SCAGILE: Tasks Requiring the Help of Security Experts 8
SCFPSSD: Manage Security Risk Inherent in the Use of Third-Party Components
SCSIC: Peer Reviews and Security Testing

policy_description: PW.5.1: Follow all secure coding practices that are appropriate to the development languages and environment to meet the organizations requirements.
reference: SCFPSSD: Establish Log Requirements and Audit Practices, Use Code Analysis Tools to Find Security Issues Early

policy_description: PW.6.1: Use compiler, interpreter, and build tools that offer features to improve executable security.
reference: SCFPSSD: Use Current Compiler and Toolchain Versions and Secure Compiler Options
SCSIC: Vendor Software Development Integrity Controls

policy_description: PW.6.2: Determine which compiler, interpreter, and build tool features should be used and how each should be configured, then implement and use the approved configurations.
reference: SCFPSSD: Use Current Compiler and Toolchain Versions and Secure Compiler Options
SCSIC: Vendor Software Development Integrity Controls

definition: human-readable code: source code, scripts, and any other form of code that an organization deems human-readable
scope: human-readable code
policy_description: PW.7.1: Determine whether code review (a person looks directly at the code to find issues) and/or code analysis (tools are used to find issues in code, either in a fully automated way or in conjunction with a person) should be used to find issues.
reference: SCSIC: Peer Reviews and Security Testing

scope: code subject to the organizations secure coding standards
policy_description: PW.7.2: Perform the code review and/or code analysis based on the organizations secure coding standards, and record and triage all discovered issues and recommended remediations in the development teams workflow or issue tracking system.
reference: SCAGILE: Operational Security Tasks 4, 7; Tasks Requiring the Help of Security Experts 10
SCFPSSD: Use Code Analysis Tools to Find Security Issues Early, Use Static Analysis Security Testing Tools, Perform Manual Verification of Security Features/Mitigations
SCSIC: Peer Reviews and Security Testing

scope: executable code (binaries, directly executed bytecode and source code, and any other form of code that an organization deems executable)
policy_description: PW.8.1: Determine whether executable code testing should be performed to find vulnerabilities not identified by previous reviews, analysis, or testing and, if so, which types of testing should be used.
reference: SCSIC: Peer Reviews and Security Testing

policy_description: PW.8.2: Scope the testing, design the tests, perform the testing, and document the results, including recording and triaging all discovered issues and recommended remediations in the development teams workflow or issue tracking system.
reference: SCAGILE: Tasks Requiring the Help of Security Experts 4, 5, 6, 7
SCFPSSD: Perform Dynamic Analysis Security Testing, Fuzz Parsers, Network Vulnerability Scanning, Perform Automated Functional Testing of Security Features/Mitigations, Perform Penetration Testing
SCSIC: Peer Reviews and Security Testing

policy_description: PW.9.1: Define a secure baseline by determining how to configure each setting that has an effect on security or a security-related setting so that the default settings are secure and do not weaken the security functions provided by the platform, network infrastructure, or services.
reference: SCAGILE: Tasks Requiring the Help of Security Experts 12
SCSIC: Vendor Software Delivery Integrity Controls
SCSIC: Vendor Software Development Integrity Controls

scope: default settings for software administrators
policy_description: PW.9.2: Implement the default settings (or groups of default settings, if applicable), and document each setting for software administrators.
reference: SCAGILE: Tasks Requiring the Help of Security Experts 12
SCFPSSD: Verify Secure Configurations and Use of Platform Mitigation
SCSIC: Vendor Software Delivery Integrity Controls
SCSIC: Vendor Software Development Integrity Controls

scope: sources of information about potential vulnerabilities in software and third-party components
policy_description: RV.1.1: Gather information from software acquirers, users, and public sources on potential vulnerabilities in the software and third-party components that the software uses, and investigate all credible reports.

scope: the softwares code
policy_description: RV.1.2: Review, analyze, and/or test the softwares code to identify or confirm the presence of previously undetected vulnerabilities.
RV.1.3: Have a policy that addresses vulnerability disclosure and remediation, and implement the roles, responsibilities, and processes needed to support that policy.

scope: each identified vulnerability
policy_description: RV.2.1: Analyze each vulnerability to gather sufficient information about risk to plan its remediation or other risk response.
reference: SCAGILE: Tasks Requiring the Help of Security Experts 10

scope: vulnerabilities to be remediated or otherwise addressed
policy_description: RV.2.2: Plan and implement risk responses for vulnerabilities.
reference: SCFPSSD: Fix the Vulnerability, Identify Mitigating Factors or Workarounds

scope: identified vulnerabilities
policy_description: RV.3.1: Analyze identified vulnerabilities to determine their root causes.
RV.3.2: Analyze the root causes over time to identify patterns, such as a particular secure coding practice not being followed consistently.

scope: the software and updates
policy_description: RV.3.3: Review the software for similar vulnerabilities to eradicate a class of vulnerabilities, and proactively fix them rather than waiting for external reports.

scope: the SDLC process
policy_description: RV.3.4: Review the SDLC process, and update it if appropriate to prevent (or reduce the likelihood of) the root cause recurring in updates to the software or in new software that is created.
